title: Fog computing
competency: Explain fog computing, its relation to cloud computing and its advantages.

keywords.def: A decentralized computing layer where data, computing, storage and applications sit between the data source and the cloud.
A device near the data source that processes and stores data locally and sends only what is needed to the cloud.
The delay between sending data or a request and getting the response.
Processing data on, or right beside, the device that produces it.
Storing and accessing data and computing services (servers, storage, networking, databases, software) over the Internet, on demand.

en.text: Fog computing is an extension of the cloud. The cloud depends on network bandwidth, and billions of users sending data in and out congest it. Fog computing places fog nodes close to the data source. They process and store data locally, at the edge, and decide what needs to go on to the cloud. So there are three layers: devices at the bottom, fog nodes in the middle and the cloud at the top.

screens.title: A busy road to the capital
screens.ask: Every CCTV camera in a city sends its full video to one far-away data center. What happens?
opts: The network gets congested and responses are slow
screens.after: Too much data travelling far causes congestion and delay. Fog computing handles data nearer the cameras.

screens.title: Why fog?
paras: Fog computing is an extension of the cloud.
The cloud relies on the bandwidth of the network provider.
Billions of users send data in and out of the cloud.
So the system becomes increasingly congested.

screens.title: Fog nodes
paras: Fog nodes sit close to the data source.
They can process and store more than the end devices (sensors, phones).
They still have far less capacity than a cloud data center.
They decide what to analyse locally, at the edge, and what to push to the cloud.
So they respond faster than sending every request to the cloud.

screens.ans: Which data to analyse locally and which to push to the cloud
screens.why: p.47: fog "provides the missing link for what data needs to be pushed to the cloud" and what "can be analyzed locally".
screens.clue: It sits between devices and the cloud.

screens.text: Why does the cloud become congested?
opts: Billions of users send data in and out through limited bandwidth
Clouds are too small to store data
screens.ans: Billions of users send data in and out through limited bandwidth
screens.why: p.46: the cloud "relies heavily on the bandwidth made available".
screens.clue: Think of one road used by everybody.

screens.text: A video-surveillance system in a Bole shopping centre has 200 cameras. Using fog, what is sent to the cloud?
opts: Only important clips and alerts, after local analysis
screens.ans: Only important clips and alerts, after local analysis
screens.why: Fog nodes analyse the big video streams locally and push only what is needed (p.47 example).
screens.clue: Video is "large and cumbersome to transfer".

en.text: Fog computing is closer to end-users, has wider consumer reach and better mobility than the cloud. It lets devices connect directly, improves the quality of service, reduces latency and improves user experience. It supports the Internet of Things and real-time Bigdata operations with billions of nodes, such as video surveillance. Edge computing goes one step further and processes data on the device itself, while the cloud remains best for huge storage and long-term analysis.

A yearly sales report for all branches

screens.title: Advantages of fog computing
paras: Closer to end-users, wider consumer reach, better mobility.
Devices connect directly instead of through the network backbone.
Improves quality of service and reduces latency.
Supports IoT things: vehicles, home appliances, even clothes.
Supports real-time Bigdata with billions of nodes.

pairs: Five years of national traffic data
screens.why: Urgent tasks need the shortest distance; big long-term data needs cloud capacity.

screens.text: Activity 2.4 Q1: why use fog computing instead of sending all data to the cloud?
opts: To process time-sensitive data near its source with less delay and congestion
Because the cloud cannot store anything
Because fog is a kind of SaaS
screens.ans: To process time-sensitive data near its source with less delay and congestion
screens.why: Fog works with the cloud, handling urgent local data and sending on what is needed.

screens.text: Activity 2.4 Q2: which services become more efficient with fog?
screens.why: Real-time and data-heavy services gain most from processing close to the user.
screens.clue: Which one uses no network at all?

screens.text: A telebirr outage happens when millions pay at once on holidays. Engineers add regional servers that check payments locally and sync to the central system later. What is this, and what does it improve?
opts: Fog computing; lower latency and less congestion
screens.ans: Fog computing; lower latency and less congestion
screens.why: Processing near users and sending only what is needed to the centre is the fog idea.
screens.clue: Where does the checking now happen?

test.text: Which example of fog computing does the book give?
In Figure 2.27, which layer is in the middle?
A smart meter sends a reading every second. Which plan best uses fog computing?
opts: A local node sums the readings and sends one hourly total to the cloud
Every reading goes straight to the cloud
The meter emails each reading to the owner
test.ans: A local node sums the readings and sends one hourly total to the cloud

notes.text: p.46: fog nodes "have a higher processing and storage capability" means higher than end devices, not higher than the cloud. The lesson teaches that fog nodes have less capacity than cloud data centers; their advantage is closeness.
The book uses "at the edge" but does not define edge computing. The cloud–fog–edge comparison table, the edge key word and related items are added for clarity.
Bole shopping centre CCTV, telebirr regional servers and the task-placement sort and match are added examples.
